issues.description: The problem statement specifies that Book should have a String property named `title` (and `author`, plus optional `genres`), but the solution's Book struct declares the title property as `bookTitle`. The solution's Client and assembleBookstore use `Book(title: ...)` and access `book.title`, which is inconsistent with the Book struct's `bookTitle` property. This name mismatch will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the correct property name to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Book struct's property name match the problem statement and the usage in Client. Rename `bookTitle` to `title` in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift (and keep it as a `let`), so the memberwise initializer and property accessors are `title`. Alternatively, change all usages to consistently use `bookTitle`, but the preferred fix is to use `title` to match the problem description and examples.

issues.description: The problem statement and the client code refer to a Book's title using the identifier 'title', but the Book struct in the solution is declared with the property name 'bookTitle'. This naming mismatch (title vs. bookTitle) breaks the clear mapping between the problem requirements and the implementation, and leads to inconsistent usage in the solution (memberwise initializer and client code expect 'title').
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the Book struct property 'bookTitle' to 'title' in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift so it matches the problem statement and the rest of the code. Ensure the memberwise initializer and all usages (e.g. Client.swift) use 'title' consistently.
